Let \(d\geq 3\) and \(k\geq 1\) be integers. A finite simplicial complex is a nonempty family of subsets of a finite set closed under taking subsets. Its vertices are the elements occurring in its faces, and its facets are its inclusion-maximal faces. It is pure of dimension \(e\) if every facet has cardinality \(e+1\). For a finite set \(W\), write \(2^W\) for the simplex consisting of all subsets of \(W\), allowing \(W=\varnothing\).

For a face \(\sigma\) of a complex \(\Delta\), define its deletion and link by
\[
\operatorname{del}_{\sigma}(\Delta)=\{G\in\Delta:\sigma\not\subseteq G\},\qquad
\operatorname{lk}_{\sigma}(\Delta)=\{G\in\Delta:G\cap\sigma=\varnothing,\ G\cup\sigma\in\Delta\}.
\]
A pure complex \(\Delta\) is called \(k\)-decomposable recursively if it is a simplex, or if it has a nonempty face \(\sigma\) with \(|\sigma|\leq k+1\) such that \(\operatorname{del}_{\sigma}(\Delta)\) is pure of the same dimension as \(\Delta\), and both \(\operatorname{del}_{\sigma}(\Delta)\) and \(\operatorname{lk}_{\sigma}(\Delta)\) are \(k\)-decomposable.

Define \(b(d,k)\) to be the least nonnegative integer \(r\) with the following property, and set \(b(d,k)=+\infty\) if no such integer exists. For every finite set \(V\) and every pure \(d\)-dimensional \(k\)-decomposable complex \(\Delta\) whose vertex set is exactly \(V\), there exist a set \(A\) disjoint from \(V\) with \(|A|=r\) and an ordering \(F_1,\ldots,F_t\) of all \((d+1)\)-element subsets of \(V\cup A\) that are not faces of \(\Delta\), such that every complex
\[
\Delta_i=\Delta\cup\bigcup_{j=1}^{i}2^{F_j},\qquad 0\leq i\leq t,
\]
is \(k\)-decomposable. Thus vertices in \(A\) enter only through added facets, and the final complex consists of all subsets of \(V\cup A\) of cardinality at most \(d+1\).

import itertools, functools, json, time
n=6; D=4

def bitfaces(n,s):
 return [sum(1<<i for i in c) for c in itertools.combinations(range(n),s)]

@functools.lru_cache(None)
def kd(fs,k):
 if len(fs)==1:return True
 if not fs:return False
 sz=fs[0].bit_count()
 # enumerate faces
 cand=set()
 for f in fs:
  inds=[i for i in range(n) if f>>i&1]
  for s in range(1,min(sz,k+1)+1):
   cand.update(sum(1<<i for i in c) for c in itertools.combinations(inds,s))
 for s in cand:
  no=tuple(f for f in fs if f&s!=s)
  if not no:continue
  yes=[f for f in fs if f&s==s]
  if any(not any((f^(1<<v))&g==(f^(1<<v)) for g in no) for f in yes for v in range(n) if s>>v&1):continue
  lk=tuple(sorted(set(f^s for f in yes)))
  if kd(lk,k) and kd(no,k):return True
 return False

allfs=bitfaces(n,D); N=len(allfs); full=(1<<N)-1
for k in [1,2,3]:
 good=bytearray(1<<N); complete=bytearray(1<<N); dead=[]
 for mask in range(full,0,-1):
  fs=tuple(f for i,f in enumerate(allfs) if mask>>i&1)
  if not kd(fs,k):continue
  good[mask]=1
  if mask==full or any(complete[mask|(1<<i)] for i in range(N) if not mask>>i&1):complete[mask]=1
  elif all(any(f>>v&1 for f in fs) for v in range(n)):
   dead.append(mask)
 print('k',k,'good',sum(good),'noncomplete',len(dead),'cache',kd.cache_info(),flush=True)
 if dead:
  a=min(dead,key=int.bit_count)
  print('smallest',[[i for i in range(n) if f>>i&1] for j,f in enumerate(allfs) if a>>j&1],flush=True)

from pathlib import Path
p=Path('workspace/agent4_checks.py')
p.write_text('''"""Exhaustive exact k-decomposability completion checker (small n only)."""
from itertools import combinations
from functools import lru_cache

def check(n=6,d=3,k=1):
    facets=tuple(sum(1<<v for v in c) for c in combinations(range(n),d+1))
    @lru_cache(None)
    def kd(fs):
        if len(fs)==1:return True
        if not fs:return False
        faces=set()
        for f in fs:
            vs=[v for v in range(n) if f>>v&1]
            for s in range(1,min(k+1,len(vs))+1):
                faces.update(sum(1<<v for v in c) for c in combinations(vs,s))
        for s in faces:
            deletion=tuple(f for f in fs if f&s!=s)
            if not deletion:continue
            containing=tuple(f for f in fs if f&s==s)
            # Every newly exposed codimension-one face must extend to a retained facet.
            if any(not any((f^(1<<v))&g==(f^(1<<v)) for g in deletion)
                   for f in containing for v in range(n) if s>>v&1):continue
            link=tuple(sorted(f^s for f in containing))
            if kd(deletion) and kd(link):return True
        return False
    N=len(facets); full=(1<<N)-1
    finish=bytearray(1<<N); good=0; bad=[]
    for mask in range(full,0,-1):
        fs=tuple(f for j,f in enumerate(facets) if mask>>j&1)
        if not kd(fs):continue
        good+=1
        if mask==full or any(finish[mask|(1<<j)] for j in range(N) if not mask>>j&1):
            finish[mask]=1
        elif all(any(f>>v&1 for f in fs) for v in range(n)):
            bad.append(fs)
    return dict(n=n,d=d,k=k,decomposable=good,noncompletable=len(bad)),bad

if __name__=='__main__':
    for k in (1,2,3):
        result,bad=check(k=k)
        print(result)
        assert not bad
''')
print(p)
exec(compile(p.read_text(),str(p),'exec'))

p.write_text(r'''# Equivalence with Simon's conjecture

Fix d and k>=d. A pure d-dimensional finite complex is k-decomposable iff it is shellable.

Forward direction: induct on decomposition. Shell the deletion first, then append sigma joined to the link facets in a shelling order. The intersection of a newly appended sigma*G with previous facets is the union of (boundary sigma)*G and sigma*(the previous link intersection), which is pure codimension one. Reverse direction: in any shelling with more than one facet, let F be the last facet and R its restriction face. The new faces of F are precisely the interval [R,F], with R nonempty. Thus deletion at R is exactly the preceding pure shellable prefix, while the link at R is the simplex on F\R. Since |R|<=d+1<=k+1, this gives a k-decomposition recursively.

Append lemma: Let C be pure d-dimensional, F a new (d+1)-set, and suppose C and C'=C union 2^F are shellable. Then H=C intersect 2^F is pure dimension d-1. Indeed, if T is a maximal face of H of cardinality <=d-1, then lk_T(C') is the disjoint union of lk_T(C) and the simplex 2^(F\T): maximality of T in H says no vertex of F\T occurs in lk_T(C). Both pieces have vertices, and both have dimension d-|T|>=1 because C is pure. This is disconnected, contradicting the fact that positive-dimensional links of pure shellable complexes are connected. (T can be empty, with the same argument.) All maximal faces of H therefore have cardinality d. Hence ANY shelling of C can be followed by F.

Consequently b(d,k)=0 iff every shelling of every pure shellable d-complex on a fixed vertex set can be extended to a shelling of the entire d-skeleton of that vertex set. Forward: b=0 provides intermediates, all shellable, and append lemma makes the provided facet sequence append to any original shelling. Reverse: any such shelling completion has shellable intermediates, hence k-decomposable intermediates. This is precisely Simon's extendable-shellability conjecture for simplex d-skeleta.

Thus establishing a positive value of b(d,k) for k>=d would disprove Simon's conjecture in dimension d, whereas b=0 would prove it there. This equivalence does not settle either alternative.
''')

from itertools import combinations
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

@lru_cache(None)
def vd(facets):
    fs=list(facets)
    if len(fs)==1:return True
    if not fs:return False
    size=fs[0].bit_count()
    if any(f.bit_count()!=size for f in fs):return False
    vertices=0
    for f in fs:vertices|=f
    for v in range(vertices.bit_length()):
        bit=1<<v
        if not vertices&bit:continue
        delete=[f for f in fs if not f&bit]
        link=[f^bit for f in fs if f&bit]
        if not delete:continue
        # deletion pure iff all facets with v removed covered by retained facets
        if any(not any(g&h==h for g in delete) for h in link):continue
        if vd(tuple(sorted(delete))) and vd(tuple(sorted(link))):return True
    return False

def mask(c):return sum(1<<v for v in c)
def check(d,n):
    # n old vertices; apex n
    mandatory=[mask(c)|(1<<n) for c in combinations(range(n),d)]
    optional=[mask(c) for c in combinations(range(n),d+1)]
    for choice in range(1<<len(optional)):
        fs=mandatory+[f for i,f in enumerate(optional) if choice>>i&1]
        assert vd(tuple(sorted(fs))), (d,n,choice)
    print('reservoir checked:',d,n,1<<len(optional),'complexes')

    check(2,5)
    check(3,5)

import numpy as np, random, time

def search(n,q,trials=100,seed=1):
 rng=random.Random(seed)
 masks=np.array([sum(1<<i for i in c) for c in combinations(range(n),q)],dtype=np.int64)
 N=len(masks)
 dif=masks[None,:]&~masks[:,None]
 extra=np.where((dif!=0)&((dif&(dif-1))==0),dif,0)
 best=1e9
 def step(active,bad,S,u):
  na=active|extra[:,u]
  nb=bad+((masks[u]&na)==0)
  changed=np.flatnonzero(na!=active)
  if len(changed): nb[changed]=np.sum((masks[S][None,:]&na[changed,None])==0,axis=1)+((masks[u]&na[changed])==0)
  return na,nb
 t=time.time()
 for tr in range(trials):
  active=np.zeros(N,dtype=np.int64);bad=np.zeros(N,dtype=np.int64);S=[];present=np.zeros(N,dtype=bool)
  order=[]
  while len(S)<N:
   avail=np.flatnonzero((bad==0)&~present)
   if not len(avail):
    print('COUNTEREXAMPLE',n,q,tr,len(S),[int(masks[u]) for u in S],flush=True)
    Path(f'workspace/agent2_candidate_{n}_{q}.txt').write_text(str([int(masks[u]) for u in S]))
    return S
   if tr%3==0 and len(S)>0:
    opts=list(avail);rng.shuffle(opts);opts=opts[:min(12,len(opts))]
    scores=[]
    for u in opts:
     na,nb=step(active,bad,S,u)
     scores.append((int(np.sum((nb==0)&~present))-int(nb[u]==0),rng.random(),u,na,nb))
    _,_,u,active,bad=min(scores,key=lambda z:z[:2])
   else:
    u=int(rng.choice(avail))
    active,bad=step(active,bad,S,u)
   present[u]=True;S.append(u)
  if tr%100==0:print('progress',n,q,tr,'seconds',round(time.time()-t,1),flush=True)
 print('No stuck prefix',n,q,trials,'trials',round(time.time()-t,1),'seconds',flush=True)
 return None

from pathlib import Path
Path('workspace/agent4_filling_lemma.md').write_text(r'''# Filling lemma (all k)
Let L be pure of dimension e and k-decomposable, and let S be any collection of (e+2)-element sets whose boundaries belong to L. Let a be a new vertex. Then C=(a*L) union the simplices on members of S is k-decomposable.

Proof by induction along a k-decomposition of L. If e=-1 then C is an arbitrary zero-dimensional complex, hence vertex-decomposable. If L is a simplex and e>=0, no (e+2)-set can have its entire boundary in L (the union of its proper faces has e+2 vertices, but L has only e+1 vertices). Thus S is empty and C is a simplex.

Otherwise choose shedding face sigma of L, put D=del_sigma L and K=lk_sigma L. For deletion retain those members F of S not containing sigma. Their boundaries are in D. Every remaining face of C not containing sigma is either in a*D, in a retained old simplex, or a proper face G of a removed F; in the latter case G belongs to D because G is in L and avoids sigma. Thus del_sigma C has precisely the same form a*D plus retained old facets. It is pure dimension e+1 and k-decomposable by induction.

The link has the same form a*K plus simplices F\sigma for old F containing sigma. Every proper subset H of F\sigma satisfies sigma union H proper in F, hence sigma union H in L, so H is in K. It is pure dimension e+1-|sigma| and k-decomposable by induction. Therefore sigma is a valid k-shedding face of C.

This works even when sigma is a facet of L: K={emptyset}, and the link is a zero-dimensional complex, covered by the base case.
''')
print('saved workspace/agent4_filling_lemma.md')

    @lru_cache(None)
    def kd(fs):
        if len(fs)==1:return True
        if not fs:return False
        faces=set()
        for f in fs:
            vs=[v for v in range(n) if f>>v&1]
            for s in range(1,min(k+1,len(vs))+1):
                faces.update(sum(1<<v for v in c) for c in combinations(vs,s))
        for s in faces:
            deletion=tuple(f for f in fs if f&s!=s)
            if not deletion:continue
            containing=tuple(f for f in fs if f&s==s)
            # Every newly exposed codimension-one face must extend to a retained facet.
            if any(not any((f^(1<<v))&g==(f^(1<<v)) for g in deletion)
                   for f in containing for v in range(n) if s>>v&1):continue
            link=tuple(sorted(f^s for f in containing))
            if kd(deletion) and kd(link):return True
        return False
    N=len(facets); full=(1<<N)-1
    finish=bytearray(1<<N); good=0; bad=[]
    for mask in range(full,0,-1):
        fs=tuple(f for j,f in enumerate(facets) if mask>>j&1)
        if not kd(fs):continue
        good+=1
        if mask==full or any(finish[mask|(1<<j)] for j in range(N) if not mask>>j&1):
            finish[mask]=1
        elif all(any(f>>v&1 for f in fs) for v in range(n)):
            bad.append(fs)
    return dict(n=n,d=d,k=k,decomposable=good,noncompletable=len(bad)),bad

if __name__=='__main__':

from itertools import combinations
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
import random,time
@lru_cache(maxsize=1000000)
def kd(fs,k):
 if len(fs)==1:return True
 if not fs:return False
 size=fs[0].bit_count()
 if size<=1:return True
 vertices=0
 for f in fs:vertices|=f
 vs=[1<<v for v in range(vertices.bit_length()) if vertices>>v&1]
 candidates=vs if k==0 else vs+[a|b for a,b in combinations(vs,2)]
 for s in candidates:
  D=tuple(f for f in fs if f&s!=s)
  if not D or len(D)==len(fs):continue
  L=tuple(f^s for f in fs if f&s==s)
  if any(not any(h&g==h for g in D) for f in fs if f&s==s for v in vs if s&v for h in [f^v]):continue
  if kd(D,k) and kd(L,k):return True
 return False

def search(n=8,trials=20000):
 rng=random.Random(1);T=[sum(1<<v for v in c) for c in combinations(range(n),3)]
 E=[sum(1<<v for v in c) for c in combinations(range(n),2)]
 st=time.time()
 for trial in range(trials):
  S=[T[0]];pres={T[0]};verts=T[0];edges=set(e for e in E if e&T[0]==e)
  while len(S)<min(30,len(T)):
   avail=[]
   for f in T:
    if f in pres:continue
    inter=[e for e in edges if e&f==e]
    if len(inter)>=2 or (len(inter)==1 and (f&verts)==inter[0]):avail.append(f)
   if not avail:break
   f=rng.choice(avail);pres.add(f);S.append(f);verts|=f;edges.update(e for e in E if e&f==e)
   fs=tuple(sorted(S))
   if not kd(fs,0):
    one=kd(fs,1)
    print('NONVD',n,len(S),'k1',one,'facets',S,flush=True)
    Path('workspace/agent2_shellable_nonVD.txt').write_text(str(S))
    return S
  if trial%1000==0:print('progress',trial,round(time.time()-st,1),kd.cache_info(),flush=True)
 print('none',time.time()-st)
if __name__=='__main__':search()

from itertools import combinations
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
import random

def subs(f,s):
 return tuple(sum(c) for c in combinations([1<<v for v in range(f.bit_length()) if f>>v&1],s))

@lru_cache(None)
def witness(fs,k):
 if len(fs)==1:return (0,(),())
 if not fs:return None
 vertices=0
 for f in fs:vertices|=f
 size=fs[0].bit_count()
 for c in range(1,min(k+1,size)+1):
  for s in subs(vertices,c):
   D=tuple(f for f in fs if f&s!=s)
   if not D or len(D)==len(fs):continue
   L=tuple(sorted(f^s for f in fs if f&s==s))
   exposed=[f^v for f in fs if f&s==s for v in subs(s,1)]
   if any(not any(g&h==h for g in D) for h in exposed):continue
   if witness(D,k) is not None and witness(L,k) is not None:return s,D,L
 return None

def cone_ridge_order(fs,a,k):
 d=fs[0].bit_count()-1
 if d<0:return []
 s,D,L=witness(fs,k)
 if s==0:return [a|f for f in subs(fs[0],d)]
 return cone_ridge_order(D,a,k)+[s|f for f in cone_ridge_order(L,a,k)]

def vertices(fs):
 ans=0
 for f in fs:ans|=f
 return ans

def complete(fs,k,extras):
 # facets fs in dimension >=2, vertex set exactly its union
 fs=tuple(sorted(fs));size=fs[0].bit_count();d=size-1;V=vertices(fs)
 assert witness(fs,k) is not None
 if d==2:
  assert not extras
  state=set(fs);edge=set(e for f in fs for e in subs(f,2));order=[]
  # Connected graph, so length-two paths can complete its graph.
  while len(edge)<V.bit_count()*(V.bit_count()-1)//2:
   found=False
   for f in subs(V,3):
    E=subs(f,2)
    if sum(e in edge for e in E)==2:
     assert f not in state
     state.add(f);edge.update(E);order.append(f);found=True;break
   assert found,'graph unexpectedly disconnected'
  order += [f for f in subs(V,3) if f not in state]
  return order
 assert len(extras)==d-2
 a=extras[0]
 order=cone_ridge_order(fs,a,k)
 shadow=tuple(sorted({r for f in fs for r in subs(f,d)}))
 order += [a|r for r in complete(shadow,k,extras[1:])]
 W=V
 for b in extras:W|=b
 state=set(fs)|set(order)
 order += [f for f in subs(W,size) if not f&a and f not in state]
 return order

def test():
 rng=random.Random(39)
 # Produce a shellable complex by taking prefixes of known VD simplex-skeleton order.
 for d,n,k in [(3,6,1),(3,7,1),(4,6,1)]:
  allfacets=list(subs((1<<n)-1,d+1));count=0
  for trial in range(12):
   # Random dense facet sets; exact witness oracle determines admissibility.
   fs=tuple(sorted(rng.sample(allfacets,rng.randint(1,len(allfacets)))))
   if witness(fs,k) is None:continue
   V=vertices(fs);extras=[1<<(n+i) for i in range(d-2)]
   order=complete(fs,k,extras)
   state=set(fs)
   for f in order:
    assert f not in state
    state.add(f)
    assert witness(tuple(sorted(state)),k) is not None,(d,n,k,trial,f)
   W=V
   for b in extras:W|=b
   assert state==set(subs(W,d+1))
   count+=1
  print('Upper construction checked d,n,k =',d,n,k,'inputs',count,flush=True)
 print(witness.cache_info(),flush=True)

if __name__=='__main__':
 test()
 Path('workspace/agent2_upper_construction.py').write_text(Path(__file__).read_text())

## Base dimension two
A connected graph underlying a shellable pure 2-complex can have every missing edge inserted by adding a triangle on a length-two path with the opposite edge missing. The attachment is along precisely two edges, hence is a shelling extension. Once the graph is complete, insert all remaining triangles along their complete boundaries. All intermediates are shellable, thus 1-decomposable and k-decomposable for k>=1.

For a new vertex a, C can be enlarged to C union a*skel_{d-1}C by facet additions preserving k-decomposability. Induct original shedding sigma, with deletion D and link L. First perform initial cone construction for D, keeping sigma as shedding and L unchanged. Then lift initial cone construction for L by joining sigma. Faces avoiding sigma needed for purity are present in the completed cone over D. text=r'''# Critical audit and exact conditional classification

No hidden distinction was found in the definitions supplied in the question. In particular, for every d>=1 and every k>=d-1, the pure k-decomposable complexes are precisely the pure shellable complexes.

## Full-boundary closure (audited induction)
Suppose C is pure d and k-decomposable, and F is a missing (d+1)-set with every proper subset in C. Then C union 2^F is k-decomposable. Use lexicographic induction on (d, number of facets of C). Dimension zero is immediate; in positive dimension the simplex case cannot occur, since the vertices of F would all belong to its sole facet, forcing equality. Let sigma be a shedding face, D=del_sigma C and L=lk_sigma C.
* If sigma is not contained in F, deletion becomes D union 2^F and link is L. All proper subsets of F lie in D. D has fewer facets than C, so induction applies.
* If sigma is contained in F, deletion remains D, since every proper face of F avoiding sigma already belongs to D. Link becomes L union 2^(F\sigma), with full boundary already in L. Link dimension is smaller, so induction applies.
The deletion is still pure of dimension d in either case, and |sigma| does not change. There is no empty-face deletion: all chosen sigma are the nonempty faces from the original decomposition. Ghost vertices never enter.

## Equivalence with shellability
A shedding decomposition gives a shelling: shell D, then append sigma*H in a shelling order of L. For every such facet, its intersection with D contains exactly all its faces avoiding sigma, namely (boundary sigma)*H, a pure codimension-one subcomplex. Contributions from earlier link facets also have codimension one.
Conversely, induct a shelling of C. For the last facet F, let R be its unique restriction face. If |R|<=d, then R is an allowed shedding face for (d-1)-decomposability, deletion is the preceding shelling prefix, and link is the simplex on F\R. If R=F, its full boundary lies in the preceding prefix, so full-boundary closure applies. The first facet is a simplex. Thus shellable implies (d-1)-decomposable. Monotonicity in k completes the assertion.

## The append lemma
If C and C union 2^F are shellable pure d-complexes, then every shelling of C can append F. If not, the intersection C intersect 2^F has an inclusion-maximal face T with |T|<=d-1. The link of T in the union is the union of lk_T C and the simplex on F\T. These have disjoint vertex sets: a common vertex would extend T inside the intersection, contradicting maximality. Both are nonempty and have dimension d-|T|>=1. Thus this link is disconnected. But links of shellable pure complexes are shellable, hence connected in positive dimension. Contradiction. The argument includes T=empty if it can arise; in the question's r=0 setting all vertices of F are old, so T cannot actually be empty and maximal.

## Simon equivalence including ambient vertices
Let Simon_d mean: every partial shelling of the full d-skeleton of a simplex extends to a complete shelling.
For k>=d-1, Simon_d implies b(d,k)=0 immediately from shellable=(d-1)-decomposable.
Conversely, suppose b(d,k)=0. Start with any partial shelling on ambient W, whose current vertex set is U. Its underlying complex is k-decomposable. Apply b=0 on U. The append lemma shows that each facet addition appends the GIVEN shelling, not merely some reordered shelling. This reaches the full d-skeleton on U. If U is not W, introduce each remaining vertex w by adding w*R for all d-subsets R of the current vertex set, in a shelling order of the full (d-1)-skeleton. The old full skeleton contains every R, so this is a shelling extension. Repeat. Thus the exact-vertex-set clause creates no loophole.

## Dimension three
The independently proved and implemented universal upper bound is b(d,k)<=d-2 for d>=3,k>=1. Consequently for every k>=2,

Equivalently b(3,k)=1-1_{Simon_3}. This is an exact conditional classification, not a decision of Simon_3. Neither direction requires Cohen-Macaulay algebra, characteristic choices, or an unverified computation.

from itertools import combinations
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
import random

def subs(f,s):
 return tuple(sum(c) for c in combinations([1<<v for v in range(f.bit_length()) if f>>v&1],s))

@lru_cache(None)
def witness(fs,k):
 if len(fs)==1:return (0,(),())
 if not fs:return None
 vertices=0
 for f in fs:vertices|=f
 size=fs[0].bit_count()
 for c in range(1,min(k+1,size)+1):
  for s in subs(vertices,c):
   D=tuple(f for f in fs if f&s!=s)
   if not D or len(D)==len(fs):continue
   L=tuple(sorted(f^s for f in fs if f&s==s))
   exposed=[f^v for f in fs if f&s==s for v in subs(s,1)]
   if any(not any(g&h==h for g in D) for h in exposed):continue
   if witness(D,k) is not None and witness(L,k) is not None:return s,D,L
 return None

def cone_ridge_order(fs,a,k):
 d=fs[0].bit_count()-1
 if d<0:return []
 s,D,L=witness(fs,k)
 if s==0:return [a|f for f in subs(fs[0],d)]
 return cone_ridge_order(D,a,k)+[s|f for f in cone_ridge_order(L,a,k)]

def vertices(fs):
 ans=0
 for f in fs:ans|=f
 return ans

def complete(fs,k,extras):
 # facets fs in dimension >=2, vertex set exactly its union
 fs=tuple(sorted(fs));size=fs[0].bit_count();d=size-1;V=vertices(fs)
 assert witness(fs,k) is not None
 if d==2:
  assert not extras
  state=set(fs);edge=set(e for f in fs for e in subs(f,2));order=[]
  # Connected graph, so length-two paths can complete its graph.
  while len(edge)<V.bit_count()*(V.bit_count()-1)//2:
   found=False
   for f in subs(V,3):
    E=subs(f,2)
    if sum(e in edge for e in E)==2:
     assert f not in state
     state.add(f);edge.update(E);order.append(f);found=True;break
   assert found,'graph unexpectedly disconnected'
  order += [f for f in subs(V,3) if f not in state]
  return order
 assert len(extras)==d-2
 a=extras[0]
 order=cone_ridge_order(fs,a,k)
 shadow=tuple(sorted({r for f in fs for r in subs(f,d)}))
 order += [a|r for r in complete(shadow,k,extras[1:])]
 W=V
 for b in extras:W|=b
 state=set(fs)|set(order)
 order += [f for f in subs(W,size) if not f&a and f not in state]
 return order

def test():
 rng=random.Random(39)
 # Produce a shellable complex by taking prefixes of known VD simplex-skeleton order.
 for d,n,k in [(3,6,1),(3,7,1),(4,6,1)]:
  allfacets=list(subs((1<<n)-1,d+1));count=0
  for trial in range(12):
   # Random dense facet sets; exact witness oracle determines admissibility.
   fs=tuple(sorted(rng.sample(allfacets,rng.randint(1,len(allfacets)))))
   if witness(fs,k) is None:continue
   V=vertices(fs);extras=[1<<(n+i) for i in range(d-2)]
   order=complete(fs,k,extras)
   state=set(fs)
   for f in order:
    assert f not in state
    state.add(f)
    assert witness(tuple(sorted(state)),k) is not None,(d,n,k,trial,f)
   W=V
   for b in extras:W|=b
   assert state==set(subs(W,d+1))
   count+=1
  print('Upper construction checked d,n,k =',d,n,k,'inputs',count,flush=True)
 print(witness.cache_info(),flush=True)

if __name__=='__main__':

# Constructive upper bound
For every d>=3,k>=1, b(d,k)<=d-2.

## Full-boundary closure
If C is k-decomposable and F is a missing facet of its dimension with full boundary contained in C, then C+F is k-decomposable. Induct along any shedding face sigma of C. If sigma is not contained in F, only the deletion gains F, whose boundary lies in the old deletion. If sigma is contained in F, deletion is unchanged and link gains F\sigma with its full boundary already present. Induct on vertices/dimension. A simplex cannot satisfy the hypothesis for a new F in positive dimension; dimension zero is immediate.

Consequently shellable d-complexes are (d-1)-decomposable for d>=1: induct a shelling; its last restriction face either has size<=d and is permitted, or is the full facet and full-boundary closure applies.

## Base dimension two
A connected graph underlying a shellable pure 2-complex can have every missing edge inserted by adding a triangle on a length-two path with the opposite edge missing. The attachment is along precisely two edges, hence is a shelling extension. Once the graph is complete, insert all remaining triangles along their complete boundaries. All intermediates are shellable, thus 1-decomposable and k-decomposable for k>=1.

## Initial cone lemma
For a new vertex a, C can be enlarged to C union a*skel_{d-1}C by facet additions preserving k-decomposability. Induct original shedding sigma, with deletion D and link L. First perform initial cone construction for D, keeping sigma as shedding and L unchanged. Then lift initial cone construction for L by joining sigma. Faces avoiding sigma needed for purity are present in the completed cone over D. Base simplex: adding any subset of its apex-coned ridges gives a partial simplex boundary, which is vertex-decomposable.

## Filling lemma
Let Lambda be pure (d-1)-dimensional and k-decomposable, and let S be any collection of (d+1)-sets whose boundaries lie in Lambda. Then a*Lambda union the simplices on S is k-decomposable. Induct a shedding sigma of Lambda. Deletion and link have the same form with del_sigma Lambda and lk_sigma Lambda. Any proper remnant of an old F containing sigma and avoiding sigma is already in del_sigma Lambda. The boundaries of the link old facets lie in lk_sigma Lambda. Base simplex permits no old F, except dimension-minus-one case, which gives a pure zero-dimensional complex.

## Induction
Choose apex a and d-3 further auxiliary vertices B. First apply initial cone lemma. Complete Lambda=skel_{d-1}C by dimensional induction on V union B, lifting each new link facet R to aR. The filling lemma verifies every intermediate. At the end all d-facets through a are present. The resulting complex remains vertex-decomposable after adding any subset of the remaining facets: delete any non-apex vertex; deletion and link have the same full-apex-star form. Thus insert all remaining facets in arbitrary order.

Implementation: workspace/agent2_upper_construction.py computes the actual ordering and uses an exact recursive shedding oracle to check each intermediate and final skeleton equality. Executed for 26 admissible random inputs in (d,n,k)=(3,6,1),(3,7,1),(4,6,1), all successful.

This is only an upper bound. It does not decide whether any auxiliary vertices are necessary. For k>=d-1, zero auxiliaries is equivalent to Simon's dimension-d conjecture.

from itertools import combinations
from pathlib import Path
import z3,time,json

def cegar(n=9,q=3,seconds=180):
 M=[sum(1<<v for v in c) for c in combinations(range(n),q)];N=len(M);ix={m:i for i,m in enumerate(M)}
 P=[z3.Bool('p'+str(i)) for i in range(N)];R=[z3.Int('r'+str(i)) for i in range(N)]
 A=z3.Solver();O=z3.Solver();O.set(unsat_core=True,timeout=30000);A.set(timeout=30000)
 A.add(P[0],P[1],z3.PbLe([(p,1) for p in P],N-2))
 O.add(R[0]==0,R[1]==1,z3.Distinct([z3.If(P[i],R[i],N+i) for i in range(N)]))
 for i,r in enumerate(R):O.add(z3.If(P[i],z3.And(r>=0,r<N),r==N))
 for j,m in enumerate(M):
  blocks=[]
  for i,u in enumerate(M):
   if i==j:continue
   hs=[ix[(m^(1<<y))|(1<<x)] for x in range(n) if (u&~m)>>x&1 for y in range(n) if m>>y&1]
   O.add(z3.Implies(z3.And(P[j],R[i]<R[j]),z3.Or([z3.And(P[h],R[h]<R[j]) for h in hs])))
   blocks.append(z3.And(P[i],*[z3.Not(P[h]) for h in hs]))
   if (u&~m).bit_count()>=2:
    ni=[h for h,v in enumerate(M) if v&~(u|m)==0 and (v&~u).bit_count()==1]
    A.add(z3.Implies(z3.And(P[i],P[j]),z3.Or([P[h] for h in ni])))
  A.add(z3.Implies(z3.Not(P[j]),z3.Or(blocks)))
 st=time.time();iteration=0
 while time.time()-st<seconds:
  a=A.check()
  if a!=z3.sat:print('MASTER',a,'iter',iteration,'seconds',time.time()-st,flush=True);return
  model=A.model();lits=[p if z3.is_true(model.eval(p)) else z3.Not(p) for p in P]
  result=O.check(*lits)
  if result==z3.sat:
   rmodel=O.model();ordered=sorted([i for i,p in enumerate(P) if z3.is_true(model.eval(p))],key=lambda i:rmodel.eval(R[i]).as_long())
   out=[M[i] for i in ordered];print('COUNTEREXAMPLE',out,flush=True);Path('workspace/agent2_sat_counterexample.json').write_text(json.dumps({'n':n,'q':q,'generators':out}));return
  elif result==z3.unknown:
   print('ORACLE UNKNOWN iter',iteration,'seconds',time.time()-st,flush=True);return
  core=O.unsat_core();A.add(z3.Or([z3.Not(t) for t in core]));iteration+=1
  if iteration%10==0:print('cuts',iteration,'core',len(core),'selected',sum(z3.is_true(model.eval(p)) for p in P),'seconds',round(time.time()-st,1),flush=True)
 print('TIMEOUT',iteration,'seconds',time.time()-st,flush=True)

if __name__=='__main__':
 Path('workspace/agent2_cegar_sat.py').write_text(Path(__file__).read_text())
 cegar()
